title: UPI Architecture: Receiving Money Never Requires a PIN or Collect Request
source: NPCI Guidelines on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Security
content: In the UPI architecture governed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), entering your UPI PIN is STRICTLY an authorization to DEBIT funds from your account. Receiving money, refunds, cashback, or rewards NEVER requires entering a UPI PIN, scanning a QR code, or accepting a collect request. If any person or app requests your UPI PIN to credit money, it is guaranteed to be an unauthorized attempt to siphon funds.
actionable_guidance: Decline all collect requests immediately. Never enter your UPI PIN unless you intend to transfer money out. Report unauthorized collect handles in your UPI app.
en:
In the UPI architecture governed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), entering your UPI PIN is STRICTLY an authorization to DEBIT funds from your account. Receiving money, refunds, cashback, or rewards NEVER requires entering a UPI PIN, scanning a QR code, or accepting a collect request. If any person or app requests your UPI PIN to credit money, it is guaranteed to be an unauthorized attempt to siphon funds.

Actionable Steps:
Decline all collect requests immediately. Never enter your UPI PIN unless you intend to transfer money out. Report unauthorized collect handles in your UPI app.

title: UPI Collect Requests: How Attackers Disguise Debit as Credit & How They Work
source: NPCI Circular on Collect Request Security & Transaction Limits
content: A UPI Collect Request (Payer-Payee pull transaction) initiates a debit from the victim account to the requester. Fraudsters frequently disguise collect requests with deceptive descriptions such as Receive Cashback Rs. 5000, Electricity Refund, or Army Officer OLX Payment. THE GOLDEN RULE OF UPI: Receiving money NEVER requires entering your 4 or 6-digit UPI PIN, scanning a QR code, or accepting a collect request. If any prompt asks you to enter your UPI PIN, money will be deducted from your account, NOT credited.
actionable_guidance: Decline all collect requests from unknown persons. Never enter your UPI PIN to receive money. Block and report the fraudulent VPA inside your app.
steps: Understand the rule: You NEVER need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money, refunds, or cashback.
Check the button: If the screen asks for a 4 or 6-digit PIN, you are SENDING money, not receiving it.
Decline the request: Tap Decline or Reject on any unfamiliar collect request in your UPI app.
Report the handle: Select Report as Scam / Fraud inside the UPI app to flag the attacker VPA with NPCI.

title: UPI AutoPay & Recurring E-Mandate Exploitation
source: RBI Master Directions on Processing of E-Mandate for Recurring Transactions
content: UPI AutoPay allows recurring debits (up to Rs. 15,000 without 2FA per cycle) once an initial mandate is authorized with a UPI PIN. Scammers trick users into approving a 'verification mandate' claiming it is a one-time security check or loan approval requirement. Once authorized, the attacker can schedule automated deductions without further user notification or PIN prompts.
actionable_guidance: Never authorize an AutoPay mandate for refunds, prizes, or customer support verification. Check 'AutoPay / Mandates' in your UPI app settings and revoke any unfamiliar recurring mandates immediately.

title: QR Code Payment Architecture: Scan to Pay Only
source: NPCI UPI QR Code Specification & Security Best Practices
content: A standard Bharat QR or UPI QR code encodes a deep link containing payee parameters (e.g., `upi://pay?pa=merchant@bank&pn=MerchantName&am=500`). Scanning a QR code inside any UPI application ONLY initiates an outbound payment. There is no technical capability in the UPI protocol to 'receive' money by scanning a QR code. Fraudsters send QR codes over WhatsApp or OLX claiming 'Scan this QR to receive payment'.
actionable_guidance: Never scan a QR code sent to you to receive payment for goods or services. To receive money, only share your phone number or UPI VPA; scanning is never required.

title: UPI Virtual Payment Address (VPA) Structure & Verification
source: NPCI UPI Operating Regulations
content: A UPI ID (VPA) consists of a username and a Payment Service Provider (PSP) bank handle in the format `username@bankhandle` (e.g., `name@oksbi`, `user@ybl`, `mobile@paytm`). Genuine merchant accounts display verified merchant names registered with NPCI. Fraudulent collect requests frequently use throwaway VPAs on open handles or mimic official names in the username prefix (e.g., `sbi.customer.helpline@icici`).
actionable_guidance: Verify the payee's actual registered bank name displayed by the UPI app before confirming any payment, not just the custom display name provided by the sender.

title: Reporting Cyber Fraud: National Helpline 1930 & Golden Hour Freezing
source: Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) — Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System
content: If you have entered your PIN, shared an OTP, or transferred money to a scammer, immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline number 1930 or register at https://cybercrime.gov.in. Under the CFCFRMS protocol, reporting within the Golden Hour (first 2-3 hours) enables police and financial intermediaries to coordinate and freeze illicit funds in intermediate mule bank accounts before cash withdrawal. What to prepare before calling 1930: (1) 12-digit transaction UTR / reference number, (2) Debit bank name and account number, (3) Fraudulent beneficiary account or UPI ID, (4) Exact date and timestamp of the transaction, (5) Screenshots of fraudulent SMS, WhatsApp chats, or payment confirmation.
actionable_guidance: Call 1930 immediately with your 12-digit UTR, debit account, and scammer UPI ID ready. Follow up on cybercrime.gov.in within 24 hours.
steps: Call 1930 immediately to connect with the National Cyber Crime Reporting Desk.
Have your details ready: 12-digit UTR number, debit bank name, transaction time, and scammer UPI ID / phone number.
The officer generates a financial fraud ticket and alerts the beneficiary bank to freeze funds.
Within 24 hours, visit cybercrime.gov.in to upload transaction screenshots, SMS evidence, and complete formal complaint registration.

If you have entered your PIN, shared an OTP, or transferred money to a scammer, immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline number 1930 or register at https://cybercrime.gov.in. Under the CFCFRMS protocol, reporting within the Golden Hour (first 2-3 hours) enables police and financial intermediaries to coordinate and freeze illicit funds in intermediate mule bank accounts before cash withdrawal. What to prepare before calling 1930: (1) 12-digit transaction UTR / reference number, (2) Debit bank name and account number, (3) Fraudulent beneficiary account or UPI ID, (4) Exact date and timestamp of the transaction, (5) Screenshots of fraudulent SMS, WhatsApp chats, or payment confirmation.

title: Step-by-Step Formal Complaint Filing on Cybercrime.gov.in
source: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), MHA
content: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (https://cybercrime.gov.in) enables citizens to lodge formal complaints for financial cyber fraud. Filing an official report generates an Acknowledgement Number which is legally mandatory for insurance claims, police investigation, and bank dispute reversals. What to prepare before filing: (1) Soft copy of bank account statement showing debited transaction, (2) Screenshots of SMS, WhatsApp messages, or call logs, (3) Suspect details (phone number, UPI ID, email, website link), (4) Identity proof (Aadhaar or Voter ID).
actionable_guidance: Visit cybercrime.gov.in, select Report Financial Fraud, fill transaction and suspect details, upload screenshots, and save your Acknowledgement PDF.
steps: Visit the official portal at https://cybercrime.gov.in and click Report Crime -> Financial Fraud.
Register/log in using your mobile number and OTP.
Prepare and enter incident details: Incident date/time, victim bank account, and 12-digit transaction UTR number.
Enter suspect details: Scammer phone number, UPI ID, bank account, or fake website URL.
Upload evidence: Bank statement copy, screenshots of messages/calls, and save your Acknowledgement Number.

title: Digital Evidence Preservation Guidelines for Fraud Victims
source: Indian Evidence Act (Section 65B) & CERT-In Citizen Advisory
content: When victimized by digital financial fraud, destroying evidence (such as deleting suspicious SMS, call logs, or WhatsApp chats in panic) hinders recovery. Under legal standards, electronic evidence requires timestamps, sender headers, recipient details, and transaction reference (UTR/RRN) numbers.
actionable_guidance: Do not delete SMS or WhatsApp chats. Take screenshots showing full phone numbers, dates, timestamps, and message headers. Export chat history and note the exact 12-digit UPI UTR number from your bank passbook.

title: RBI Zero Liability Policy for Unauthorized Electronic Banking Transactions
source: RBI Master Circular DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18
content: Under RBI regulations, a customer has ZERO LIABILITY for unauthorized electronic banking transactions where the fraud or deficiency lies within the banking system, or in third-party breaches where the customer notifies the bank within 3 working days of receiving the debit alert. If notified within 4 to 7 working days, liability is limited to Rs. 10,000 for savings accounts.
actionable_guidance: Immediately notify your bank in writing (via email and registered helpline) within 72 hours of any unauthorized debit to establish zero-liability eligibility. Keep written complaint ticket numbers.

title: Remote Desktop Screen Sharing Fraud: What to Do if an App Was Installed
source: Cyber Crime Investigation Cell & RBI Advisory on Social Engineering
content: Scammers pose as bank customer support, courier executives, or utility officers and trick victims into installing remote desktop software (AnyDesk, TeamViewer QuickSupport, RustDesk, AirDroid). (4) Call your bank to freeze netbanking and check for unauthorized debits. (5) Scan your device using Google Play Protect.

Run a malware scan using Google Play Protect before re-enabling internet.

title: Digital Arrest & Fake Police / Customs Narcotics Extortion: Legal Facts
source: Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), CBI, & Delhi Police Cyber Crime Cell Advisory
content: Scammers pose as CBI officers, Cyber Crime Police, FedEx/DHL courier customs officials, or judges. They claim that an illegal parcel containing narcotics/passports was intercepted in your name, and place you under a fake Digital Arrest on Skype or WhatsApp video call. They threaten arrest unless you transfer funds to an RBI verification account for asset clearance. STATUTORY LEGAL REALITY: (1) Indian Law (Code of Criminal Procedure / Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita Section 35) does NOT recognize any concept of Digital Arrest. (2) Real law enforcement agencies NEVER interrogate or place suspects under arrest over video calls. (3) No government body or court demands money transfers to safe accounts or RBI clearance accounts. (4) Disconnect immediately and call 1930.
actionable_guidance: Do not panic. Disconnect the video call immediately. Real police never arrest via Skype or WhatsApp. Report the caller number to 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in.

Report to 1930: Call the 1930 National Cyber Helpline or file an extortion report on cybercrime.gov.in.

title: 'Accidental Money Transfer' Social Engineering Trap
source: RBI Consumer Education and Protection Department Advisory
content: The victim receives a fake bank credit SMS or an actual small transfer (e.g., Rs. 5,000) from an unknown number. Soon after, a distressed caller phones claiming: 'I mistakenly sent my child's hospital fee to your UPI ID, please return it urgently via Google Pay'. If the victim sends money back to the caller's separate UPI ID, the scammer files a formal unauthorized transaction chargeback with their own bank, causing the bank to debit the original sum again. The victim loses twice or becomes implicated in money laundering.
actionable_guidance: Never send money back directly via UPI. Tell the caller to contact their bank to initiate formal inter-bank auto-reversal. Inform your own bank branch in writing that you received unsolicited funds and authorize the bank to reverse it through official banking settlement channels.

title: The HTTPS Padlock Fallacy: Encryption Does NOT Guarantee Legality

content: A common misconception is that a website with a padlock icon (`https://`) is legitimate and safe. actionable_guidance: Never rely solely on the padlock icon to judge website legitimacy. Verify the exact spelled domain name and look for official domain registration.

title: Golden Hour Protocol: What to Do Immediately When Money is Lost to a Scam
source: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Circular on Customer Protection & I4C MHA Advisory
content: When money has been wrongfully deducted or transferred in a scam, acting in the Golden Hour (the first 1-2 hours) is critical to stopping the funds from being laundered. Immediate multi-step protocol: (1) Call your bank emergency helpline immediately to freeze your account/cards and log an unauthorized transaction report. Under RBI Zero-Liability guidelines, notifying within 3 days limits customer liability for unauthorized third-party breaches. (2) Call 1930 (National Cyber Helpline) immediately to initiate inter-bank beneficiary account freezing. (3) Block your UPI IDs and netbanking access. (4) Preserve all digital evidence: screenshots of debit SMS, chat history, call logs, and UTR numbers. (5) Lodge a formal complaint on https://cybercrime.gov.in to receive a police acknowledgement number.

title: How to Block, Disable, or De-link a UPI ID

content: If you suspect your UPI ID has been compromised or you want to prevent further electronic debits: (1) Block within UPI Apps: In PhonePe (Profile -> Payment Settings -> UPI IDs -> Delete), in Google Pay (Profile -> Bank Account -> Manage UPI IDs -> Trash icon), in Paytm (Profile -> UPI & Payment Settings -> Manage UPI ID -> Remove). (3) Emergency Bank SMS: Many banks offer emergency SMS blocking (e.g. SBI: SMS BLOCK UPI to bank shortcode, HDFC: SMS BLOCK or via NetBanking Security). (4) De-register from UPI: De-link all bank accounts from third-party payment apps.

source: RBI Circular on Customer Protection: Limiting Liability in Unauthorized Electronic Banking (DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18)
en:
